raw_response:
I farm 19.1 mu, so I do not run it like a tiny household plot. I still count every yuan, but on this size I will put enough fertilizer and water so I do not lose yield for saving a little money. I have done this 15 years, and I do not like changing too much at once. I start from what worked before, then I adjust a little by crop and by land. For my better irrigated land, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation because that is steady money and I know how to manage it. For the rest, I will plant cotton because it spreads my risk and fits our labor if I manage sprays on time. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too fancy, but I do look at what nearby good growers do, and if an improved or hybrid seed gave good stand and good yield in the village, I will use that. Wheat and maize are my main grain crops, so I will feed them enough nitrogen first, then add phosphorus and some potassium so the crop does not go weak. Cotton can hold on a bit, but if I want bolls and not just tall plants, I will still put real fertilizer under it and keep water steady. Because I have well irrigation, I will not wait too long if the field is dry. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and one more watering than watch yield fall. On pests, wheat and maize usually need fewer sprays for me, but cotton I will watch closely and spray more times if insects come hard.
